A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel adaptive scheduling technique for loops that is based on runtime information of load and processor affinity, and have shown that it is effective for improving the performance of parallel loops.

we propose an adaptive scheduling mechanism that uses runtime information to dynamically adjust scheduling granularity for parallel loops in distributed shared-memory systems, and we show that the proposed algorithm and its variations outperform several existing scheduling algorithms.

the adaptive scheduling algorithm and the adaptive scheduling algorithm with the control mechanism of the adaptive scheduling granularity (ASG) are the most effective and efficient scheduling algorithms for parallel loops.

the scheduling granularity should be adapted at runtime to match the real workload distribution of a parallel loop.
adaptive scheduling algorithms can improve performance by using runtime information.
